rationale: No country variable in the dictionary; the ISO3 code (CRI) is a constant assigned by the harmonizer.
No survey year variable exists; the reference period (e.g. July 2021-June 2022 in the victimization questions) is only mentioned in question text, so the year is a constant.
The dictionary has no interview month variable.
region holds the six planning regions, the first-level administrative division, and can be used directly.
zona has 1=Urbana, 2=Rural and must be recoded to 1=urban, 0=rural.
No single household ID exists; it must be built from the questionnaire/dwelling identifiers and the household number (id_vivienda and id_hogar are only flags).
linea is the person line number within the household.
factor is the only expansion weight, so it is used for households (kept where id_hogar=1).
factor is the only expansion weight and is applied to persons.
upm is the primary sampling unit variable.
No explicit stratum variable exists; UPM (primary sampling unit) is the closest design variable, though region/zona could define strata, so this is a weak proxy.
a3 gives relationship to the household head and is recoded into head, spouse, child (including stepchildren), other relative, non-relative and domestic worker.
a4 records sex directly with 1=Hombre and 2=Mujer, matching the target codes.
a5 is age in completed years, with special codes 98/99 for ignored age to be set missing.
a6 marital status is recoded: union libre and casado to 2, divorciado and separado to 3, viudo to 4, soltero to 1.
The dictionary has no question on ethnicity or race, so this would be coded as not asked.
a8a (with a8b as secondary mention) identifies persons with a permanent limitation, so disability is 1 when a8a is 1-7 and 0 when it is 0.
condmig=2 (external migrant) or lugnac codes 2-4 and 8 indicate birth abroad; the survey measures the mother's residence at birth, so this is an approximation of international migrant.
condact gives employed, unemployed, and inactive, and age a5 is used to assign below working age (the survey's cutoff is 15, with condact apparently covering ages 15+).
posiemppri gives position in main job (employer 21, own account 22, employee 11/12, unpaid 13), mapped to employer, own_account, employee and unpaid.
Main-job occupation at COCR 2011 one-digit level (10 groups) is recoded to the IDB occupation groups, with code 10 (not well specified) treated as missing.
Main-job industry (CAECR 2011 sections) is collapsed to the 9 IDB industry groups.
Hours in the main job are available as effective hours (horefepri, the reference-week default in IDB) or normal hours (hornorpri), with 999 set to missing.
Total effective hours across all jobs (hortotefe) is available, with total normal hours as an alternative; 999 is set to missing.
Establishment size in c10 is recoded to small/medium/large, but the dictionary shows only the upper categories (10 and up), so the lower bins are likely present in the full code list.
The institutional sector of the main job (secinspri, code 3 = general government) or secfuerzatrab (codes 1-2 = public sector) identifies public employment.
There is no written-contract question, so contract type has to be proxied from job stability (e1/estabili) among wage earners, which is only an approximation.
Current contribution is best proxied by social-security deductions from the salary (e10a), complemented by the insurance type (a11) and pension scheme contribution (a12).
Insurance status (a11) distinguishes the uninsured (0) from the various types of social security coverage.

The survey provides a derived main-job income (ipbt gross, ipnt net, with salary and independent components) which can be used directly for monetary labor income in the main job, excluding the non-monetary parts.
Non-monetary income of the main job is the total non-monetary salary (tspnm, built from spnma/spnmv/spnmt/spnmvh/spnmo) plus non-monetary independent income (inmpina, inmpia), or alternatively ipinm.

Monetary income of the second job is the secondary salary (issb, or ssmb) plus secondary independent income (isit); this assumes isit includes the non-monetary part, otherwise use ssif/gsi components.

Total monetary labor income is the gross labor income total (itrbt) net of non-monetary parts, or built as main plus secondary monetary components (ipim, ipsmb, issb, isit); the choice between gross and net is a convention.
Total non-monetary labor income combines main-job non-monetary independent income (ipinm), non-monetary salary (tspnm) and secondary-job non-monetary income (inmsi, ssnm).
Monetary non-labor income is property income (irp) plus total monetary transfers (ttm), which includes pensions and remittances.

Pension income comes from national pensions (ttpn, tpn plus aguinaldo tapn) and foreign pensions (ttpe, tpe plus tape); contributory status is not separated from the non-contributory RNC pension, which is excluded.
Remittances are the transfers from abroad (te), derived from h9k1 with its period h9k2.
Imputed rent is the self-reported rent the household would pay (v2b), applied to owner-occupied dwellings identified by v2a.
lp is the official poverty line value.
The official extreme poverty line is the basic food basket value (cba).
a13 codes current attendance in formal education, with 0=No asiste, so attendance is a13 in 1-8 (education types), with 9 (non-formal education) and 99 treated as not attending or missing.
escolari directly gives years of schooling; a14 or nivinst could serve as a fallback.
a15a gives the type of school attended (1=Público), conditioned on current attendance from a13.
v11 gives piped water supply (1-3 vs 0), while v12 can help refine whether the source is a public network.
v12 gives the source of drinking water (aqueduct, well, river, rain), and v11 can help distinguish piping location.
v15 records electricity availability (0=none, 1-5 grid or private plant), though it asks about electricity in the dwelling rather than specifically lighting.
v13a gives the type of sanitation system, v13b/v14b give whether it is shared, and v14a gives whether the dwelling has a bathroom.
v6 is the predominant floor material.
v3 is the predominant exterior wall material.
v4 is the predominant roof material.
v8 is the count of rooms used only for sleeping; recode 99 (ignorado) to missing.
v9 gives total aposentos in the dwelling, excluding bathrooms, hallways and garage but including bedrooms; 99 is missing.
v2a tenure: 1 and 2 (owned, fully paid or paying in installments) map to owned=1, 3 (rented) to 0, and 4 (precario) and 5 (cedida/prestada) to occupied de facto=3; 9 is missing.
v19 asks directly whether the dwelling has internet service (1=yes, 0=no); 9 is missing.
v18a indicates whether the household has a mobile phone (1=yes, 2=no), so recode to 1/0; the count variable v18a1 could be used as a cross-check.
Household owns a computer if it has either a laptop (v18f, 3=yes) or a desktop (v18g, 5=yes); tablets (v18q) are excluded.
v18c records ownership of a refrigerator (5=yes, 6=no).
v18j records ownership of a car not used for work (3=yes, 4=no); v18j1 gives the count.
